text:
Hi,

Sonnbühl Management Ltd in Schwyz has let me go. Tom Tanner, the operations manager, gave me the letter on 5 June 2026 and I signed for it the next morning. I'd only been there since the beginning of April.

My contract is attached as well. Please look at the part about notice, because that's where Mr Tanner and I don't agree. My written contract says two months' notice to the end of a month. I know that in the first year the normal rule is just one month, but my contract sets two, and I signed it that way on purpose because I gave up a secure job to move here.

Mr Tanner's letter, which I've also attached, has me finishing at the end of August. He says that's generous. But he has also told me my last pay will only cover June and July, because 'in the first year it's one month anyway', and he wants me to use up my holidays in August. I earn CHF 1,670 a month for my part-time post, so for me it's a lot of money.

One more thing, since a friend asked me whether pregnancy rules might help: no, that doesn't apply to me at all. I'm a man, I wasn't pregnant and I haven't had a baby.

I'd like to know who is right about the notice and how much they should actually pay me.

Thanks,
Owen Vogel
Wiesenstrasse 27, Schwyz

Sonnbühl Management Ltd
Schwyz

Schwyz, 5 June 2026

Termination of employment

We hereby give notice to terminate your employment with Sonnbühl Management Ltd. Your employment will end on 31 August 2026.

Please return your keys and company phone on your last working day. Your final salary statement and your reference will be sent to you after that date.

Kind regards

Tom Tanner
Operations Manager
Sonnbühl Management Ltd

Received on 6 June 2026
Signature: O. Vogel

EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT

between Sonnbühl Management Ltd, Schwyz (employer), represented by Tom Tanner, Operations Manager,
and Owen Vogel, Wiesenstrasse 27, Schwyz (employee)

1. Start of employment: 2 April 2026, for an unlimited period.

2. Position: building services coordinator, part-time (50%).

3. Salary: CHF 1,670 gross per month.

4. Termination: either party may terminate the employment with two months' notice to the end of a calendar month. Notice must be given in writing.

Schwyz, 20 March 2026

The employer: T. Tanner
The employee: O. Vogel
